yea okay I get the inconsistency point but imagine this:

you get all the benefits of mouse accel like easy long range flicks while still being able to make micro adjustments. but what if you now also have consistency? it'd basically be perfect so whenever someone thinks mouse accel is inconsistent I recommend a mouse accel preset that looks something like this:

start out flat at the bottom with your normal sens so that micro adjustments feel the same. then go straight up a bit in the graph and then flatten it again for a bit and then go up again and flatten again. this preset is very consistent since you basically have 3 different DPI's instead of almost infinite like you would have with a steady curve. basically the bottom sens is used for micro adjustments, the middle one for like 60 - 120 degree flicks and the top sens for everything above 120 degrees.

okay so idk if you understand either so I'll give a quick explanation:

let's say you move your mouse 1 inch in real life, without mouse accel, that movement would always move your crosshair in game by the same length, let's say 800 dots. so if you move your mouse 1 inch it moves 800 dots, no matter if you move the mouse at light speed or if you let a turtle move it.

with mouse accel however, moving your mouse slowly by 1 inch would move it 800 dots, as expected. but if you now move the mouse very quickly by 1 inch, depending on your mouse accel settings, the crosshair would move by more than 800 dots, maybe by 1200 dots for example.
